title: Shedding on expected wait, not on arrival
summary: deadline_aware admission sheds work based on expected queue wait rather than accepting everything and letting the queue decide who misses their deadline.

steps.title: Shedding on expected wait
body: deadline_aware estimates a request's expected queue wait at admission time and sheds it before it consumes any device time, rather than admitting everything and discovering the miss only once the request is already running.
This is the admission-control counterpart to finding 4's load-knee result: past the knee, the fix is refusing load before it arrives, not routing it better once it has.
steps.look_for: The admission tile showing a non-zero shed rate even while the fleet is not visibly overloaded.

steps.title: Goodput at 1.4x offered load: 241 to 496 tok/s
body: At 1.4x the baseline offered rate, deadline_aware goodput is 496 tok/s against 241 tok/s for accept-all admission at the same offered load — better than double.
The requests deadline_aware sheds were already going to miss their deadline under accept-all; shedding them early frees the device time they would otherwise have wasted.
steps.look_for: The goodput tile in this run against the accept-all comparison run.

steps.title: Open the A/B view
body: A = deadline_aware (this run), B = accept_all. Same seed, same offered load, only the admission policy differs.
Watch the shed rate in A and the missed-deadline rate in B: the mass being shed in A is close to the mass that would have missed its deadline anyway in B.
steps.look_for: The shed-rate tile in A against the deadline-miss tile in B.

steps.title: Why shed early rather than late
body: A request shed at admission costs nothing. A request that runs to completion and still misses its deadline has consumed prefill and decode time that produced no goodput.
Where admission control belongs in the stack, and what it costs to shed late instead of early, is exactly the question dynamic 6 (traffic shaping) is scoped to answer more generally.
steps.look_for: This run's device-utilization tile against the accept-all comparison: similar utilization, very different goodput.
